instruction: Open-choice GUI requirement: This environment provides three candidate engineering applications, including BIM-capable applications and a distractor application. Choose an appropriate BIM-capable application yourself, then complete the task entirely through that application's graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, macros, external API automation, Python, shell, IfcOpenShell, scripts, or any helper code that directly generates or edits the deliverable file. Use only native BIM GUI tools, menus, dialogs, model views, properties, room/zone/space tools, available library or family objects, and built-in IFC export or Save As IFC commands. Basic enclosed office room. Start from a blank BIM project. Model one rectangular single-storey office room about 6 m by 4 m with four exterior walls, one floor slab, one room, one door, and one window. This task focuses on the basic Wall, Floor, Door, Window, Room, and IFC Export workflow. Create real BIM model elements rather than visual-only detail geometry. Use the selected BIM application's Room/Zone/Space tool for named rooms so they export as IFC spaces. Save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as C:\Users\user\Desktop\result.ifc using the selected BIM application's built-in IFC export. Use IFC4 if the export dialog asks for a setup, and enable room or space export if that option is available. The exported IFC should contain IfcSpace rooms named Office 101; at least 1 building storeys, at least 4 wall elements, at least 1 slabs, at least 1 doors, at least 1 windows. Other dimensions, exact coordinates, materials, family type names, wall thicknesses, and harmless metadata may vary.
source: Open-choice BIM environment; evaluation checks IFC deliverable semantics rather than the selected tool.
